title: Multimodal Mirror posterior codebook versus direct and independent modes
hypothesis: A phase codebook over a shared 16D logistic weight vector represents an equal-weight mixture of K=32 distinct modes with matched predictive NLL/diversity and lower bytes than direct coefficients or independent mode vectors.
mirror_coordinate: K scalar rotation phases over a fixed 2D subspace
logical_multiplicity: K distinct posterior predictive classifier modes, counted only by output diversity/quality

task.labels: Bernoulli sampled from equal-weight mixture of mode probabilities

controls: phase Mirror codebook plus one shared vector
direct two-coefficient codebook plus same shared state

development.selection: fixed K and code serializer; development only validates task and metrics

storage.authority: actual deterministic serialized inference payload bytes
paid_objects: shared vector or independent mode vectors

success_gate: Mirror NLL within .01 of independent exact mixture, pairwise disagreement within .02, and payload <=.80x direct coefficients.
failure_gate: Quality/diversity gate misses or byte reduction is less than 20% versus direct coefficients.
boundaries: no posterior training or mode discovery
K logical modes are not independent capacity
